title: The Job Description
logline: When GNB swallows Marshall's law firm, Arthur Hobbs becomes Barney's new boss and answers Barney's legendary 'Please.' with 'Please what?' Facing a Friday deadline to put his job in writing, a terrified Barney secretly hires Marshall as his coach, and Marshall, finally the expert on Barney's turf, turns him into a second Marshall, while Ted, Robin and Lily go undercover at GNB to steal the one page that says what Barney does.
coldOpen: Kids, in the fall of 2012, a merger gave your Uncle Barney a new boss, and for the first time in his life, Barney Stinson was scared. So he asked for help from the one man who had survived that boss for seven years.

guests.name: Merrill Toft
guests.role: A meek GNB vice president who, in Lily's version of events, has had the corner office since 1987 and hands it to a total stranger in a nice suit without a fight

scenes.summary: Monday, day three of the merger. Barney brushes off Marshall's flash cards. Arthur Hobbs arrives and shrugs off the tie compliment, the high five and the scotch, takes Barney's chair, and meets 'Please.' with 'Please what?' Barney's HR job description is the word Please. One real page by Friday at nine, or he's redundant. A Tugboat text melts Arthur for one second. Barney, numb, begs Marshall for help with a sincere please. Button: how long until Arthur liked Marshall? He'll let him know.

beats.line: Monday morning. GNB had owned Marshall's law firm for three days.
Barney, he gets here at nine. Let me prep you. I made flash cards.
Relax. Gary from Compliance named his boat after me. His second boat. The first one's named after his wife.
Barney, Arthur Hobbs was late to court once. The judge apologized.
Stinson! Feet off the desk!
Arthur! Barney Stinson. Love the tie. Purple. It says, I own a yacht and I'm furious at it.
I own two. I'm furious at both.
Ha! Up top!
Put your hands down, Stinson. This is a bank.
Scotch? I know it's early, but it's five p.m. in Dubai.
Then go to Dubai. You can be fired there too.
Stinson, I spent the weekend reviewing every position in this division. Four hundred and twelve jobs.
I understand four hundred and eleven of them.
What do you do?
Please.
Please what?
Please is the start of a sentence, Stinson. Finish it.
It doesn't have a... nobody's ever... it's less of a sentence and more of a vibe.
HR's file on you. You approved it yourself.
beats.title: GNB Job Description: B. Stinson

beats.line: One real page, on my desk Friday at nine. Or you're redundant.
See the new vending machine on nine? He was a vice president.
Oh. Oh, look at him. Tugboat met a beagle at the park. They're sharing a stick.
Stinson, repeat the word sharing and you'll be dispensing Funyuns on nine.
Marshall. I can't feel my suit.
That's the Hobbs chill. It wears off in about four years.
Teach me how to survive him. And nobody can know. Not Ted. Not Robin. Never Lily.
Barney Stinson is asking me for help. On his turf. In his office. In a suit.
Say it again. Slower.
Please. Help me.
Whoa. Was that the normal please? I didn't know you had a normal one.
Two conditions. During training, you call me Coach. And I get the big chair.
Ooh. It's still warm.
That's my fear.
Coach. How long did it take before Arthur liked you?
Seven years.
And then what happened?
I'll let you know.

scenes.summary: Monday night. Marshall's whispered Hobbs Rules at the bar: no catchphrases, legendary gets you sent to Newark, and Arthur's highest praise is 'adequate'. Lily's adequate cake blows the secret. The gang learns Barney's job must exist on paper by Friday and declares every woman for herself. Ted's secret-room theory, Lily's walked-in-and-sat-down theory (cutaway, which Barney confirms took two tries), Robin's fall-guy theory, which everyone laughs off, Barney most nervously and Marshall with a spit take. Role-play: Marshall's Arthur is terrifying. Button: plain ties.

beats.line: That night, Coach Eriksen held his first practice. At the bar. In a whisper.
The Hobbs Rules. Rule one. No catchphrases. He fined Brad four hundred dollars for saying awesome.
What about legendary?
A guy said legendary in 2010. Arthur transferred him to the Newark office.
We didn't have a Newark office. Arthur opened one.
Rule two. Arthur's highest compliment is adequate. I've gotten one. I cried in the stairwell.
And I baked him a cake that said adequate!
You told Lily?
Also, Marshall doesn't whisper. He just leans.
Wait. Barney's job is going to exist? On paper? In a building I can walk into?
I want that page. And it's every woman for herself.
I'm not a—
Every woman for herself, Ted.
Fine. But I already pulled the floor plans for the GNB building.
Your office is eleven feet shorter inside than outside. There's a room behind those posters.
It's a closet.
With its own thermostat, Barney?
Amateur. He doesn't work there at all. He walked in one day in a suit, sat down, and nobody dared to ask.
You're in my chair.
I've had this office since 1987. Who are you?
Please.
Of course. So sorry. My mistake.
Mister Stinson? Your bonus. Also, I'm your assistant now.
That's ridiculous.
It took two tries.
You're overthinking it. Banks do shady stuff. Somebody has to sign for it.
So Barney signs everything, and if it ever blows up, he goes to prison instead of the CEO.
Barney? In prison? He'd have the whole cell block in tailored jumpsuits by Tuesday.
Ha. Prison. So dumb. Hilarious. Marshall, tell me more about the dog.
Seriously, Dad?
Bad batch, kids. Carl was going through a phase.
Okay. Role-play. I'm Arthur. You just walked in.
Stinson! What do you do?
Sir! Please!
Please what?
Please don't hurt me!
Marshmallow. Do that voice again later.
You froze! Isn't it great?
Terrible, I mean. It's terrible.
Practice is at six a.m. And wear a plain tie.
Define plain.
A tie that doesn't have a name.
Every tie has a name, Marshall!

scenes.summary: Thursday, GNB's legal floor, Marshall's new cubicle. Lily has been temping as Bethany since Tuesday and got promoted twice; Ted got in by saying he's an architect; Robin has a lanyard and a flu shot. Barney arrives Marshalled: oatmeal suit, binder, offers Tugboat a hotdish. Arthur calls his memo adequate (Legen-dequate), then reveals it's Marshall's memo, smiley face and all: the committee cuts duplicates. Bethany is told to stop getting promoted. Barney and Marshall fight; Marshall admits he loved being the cool guy for once. Barney leaves. Button: Arthur finally gives Marshall his second adequate, and it only feels a little good.

beats.line: Thursday. GNB Legal, where Marshall now had a cubicle, a nameplate, and a student.
Lily?
It's Bethany. From the temp agency. I've been Bethany since Tuesday.
I've been promoted twice.
I walked up to security and said, Hi, I'm Ted Mosby, architect. And they let me in.
That has never worked before.
I told the lobby I'm doing a puff piece on the merger. I got a lanyard, a tote bag and a flu shot.
Guys, you can't be here! Barney's page goes on Arthur's desk tomorrow at nine!
So tonight, it's sitting in Barney's office. Unguarded.
Right next to the secret room.
Barney. What are you wearing?
It's just a suit, Robin. It doesn't have a name.
It's beige.
It's oatmeal.
He looks like a guy who'd help you move.
I'd love to help you move, Robin! I'll bring a cooler. And sandwiches, for after!
I made a binder, Coach. The tabs have tabs.
Stinson!
Good morning, sir! How's Tugboat, sir?
He has a little cough.
Oh no. Tell him I'm thinking about him, sir. I'll bring him a hotdish.
Stinson. Your merger memo was adequate.
Legen—
Barney!
Adequate. Thank you, sir.
It was adequate because I've read it before. Eriksen wrote it last week.
You even kept the smiley face next to the word litigation.
Eriksen. Why is Stinson doing you?
I already have one Eriksen. The merger committee cuts duplicates.
We had twins in Accounting. We kept the evil one. Better with numbers.
And Bethany. You've been promoted twice. Stop it.
Tomorrow. Nine. One page. Your page, Stinson. Not his.
You turned me into you, and now he's going to fire me for being you!
What's wrong with being me?
Nothing, if you're you! I'm wearing oatmeal, Marshall!
Every night, you're the expert, Barney. You came to me. For one week, I got to be the cool guy.
Then you should have made me better, Marshall. Not beige.
Eriksen. That memo. Adequate.
It doesn't even feel good.
It feels a little good.

scenes.summary: Friday, eight fifty-eight. Ted is knocking on the AWESOMENESS poster, Lily finds the sealed page, every woman for herself. Barney walks in back in a real suit, ready to be fired, and tells them to read it; Lily gives it back unread. Marshall apologizes and shares his expert read: Arthur fires people mid-sneeze, but he asked Barney a follow-up, and he only asks follow-ups of people he keeps (flashback: Marshall's first week, crying, 'Do you like dogs?' 'Adequate.'). Arthur arrives; Barney starts reading 'I provide legal' and Arthur stops him. Nineteen people explained their jobs; the one who said please passes. Arthur had Barney's job once, nobody ever asked, so he got a dog. The friends who keep asking are the ones who stay. Allergies, Tugboat's in Connecticut. 'Please.' in chorus. Arthur: wait for it, legendary, and fines himself. Future Ted: Marshall knew all along.

beats.line: Ted, you've been knocking on Awesomeness for ten minutes.
Found it! Top drawer. Sealed. It says, Arthur, eyes only.
Every woman for herself, Lily. Hand it over.
I am also a woman for myself!
Go ahead, read it. He's firing me at nine either way.
If I'm going out, I'm going out in Desmond.
No. Not like this.
I would have read it like this.
Barney. I was wrong. I made you into me because I liked being the expert.
But here's what I actually know. Arthur fires people mid-sentence. He once fired a guy mid-sneeze.
On Monday, you said please, and he asked a follow-up. In seven years, he's asked me exactly one.

beats.label: Marshall's first week at the firm

beats.line: Eriksen! Why are you crying?
Because you're terrifying, sir. And the copier hates me. And I miss Minnesota.
Follow-up question. Do you like dogs?
I love dogs, sir.
Adequate.
He doesn't keep the people who are good, Barney. He keeps the ones who aren't pretending.
So don't be me. Be the scared guy in the great suit.
Coach.
If anyone asks, I was coaching him.
Stinson! Why is there an architect knocking on my posters?
There's a room back there!
Next question.
Your page, Stinson. Read it.
I provide legal—
Stop!
Not in front of the architect.
Put it away. I wrote this merger. I know what all four hundred and twelve people do.
Then why make me write it down?
To see who would. Nineteen people explained their jobs to me this week. One brought slides.
What's wrong with slides?
A man who explains your job can't be trusted with it. You said please and didn't blink.
I had your job once, Stinson. Thirty years. My wife never knew. My brother never knew.
After a while, nobody even asked. So I got a dog. He never asks.
My friends ask me every single day.
Every day. It's on my calendar.
Then keep them, Stinson. The ones who keep asking are the ones who'll stay when you finally answer.
Barney, are you crying?
Allergies. Tugboat.
Tugboat's in Connecticut.
So, now can we know?
Please.
Stinson. Your review. Wait for it.
Legendary.
That's four hundred dollars. I'll be fining myself.
Seven years, sir! I got adequate!
If you need to cry, Eriksen, use the stairwell on nine. Next to the vice president.
Kids, Barney never told us what he does. Neither did Marshall, who had read Barney's file that Monday.
Marshall Eriksen has never kept a secret for more than an hour. He's kept that one for eighteen years. That's how I know it's bad.
